title: Practice 9: при- and у-: arriving, and leaving

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.why: **принёс** is the past tense (masculine) of **принести** (to bring (by foot), to fetch (transitive) to transport toward someone/somewhere); to yield, to bear) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приносить**. past: он принёс · она принесла́ · оно принесло́ · они принесли́. — Wiktionary, «принести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «приносить — принести — to bring (on foot).» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: You must come every six months for a check-up.
exercises.why: **приходить** (the infinitive) (to come (to), to arrive (at) (place, conclusion, state of abandonment, anger, insanity)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **прийти**. — Wiktionary, «приходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда? — Это старшина. Лейтенант в штабе? — Нет, он уже идёт (едет) сюда.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **уходить** (**уходить**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Hey, that knot is no good. The boat will float away.
exercises.why: **уплывёт** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **уплыть** (to swim away; to sail away) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уплывать**. future: я уплыву́ · ты уплывёшь · он уплывёт · мы уплывём · вы уплывёте · они уплыву́т. — Wiktionary, «уплыть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **приплывёт** (**приплыть**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **приводит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **приводить** (to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **привести**. present: я привожу́ · ты приво́дишь · он приво́дит · мы приво́дим · вы приво́дите · они приво́дят. — Wiktionary, «приводить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «приводить — привести — to bring (along), to lead.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **уводит** (**уводить**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **принеси** is the imperative (ты, singular) of **принести** (to bring (by foot), to fetch (transitive) to transport toward someone/somewhere); to yield, to bear) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приносить**. imperative: принеси́ · принеси́те. — Wiktionary, «принести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «приносить — принести — to bring (on foot).» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
